Somewhere within me (Andoeni Padilla, Mexico, 18m)

A story of a friendship told through childhood archival material. They try to answer who they are, who they wish to be, and inevitably, they turn to who they have been.

Unhappy Sexy Girl (Cassidy Civiero, Canada, 7m)

A transmasc filmmaker revisits his past as an unhappy sexy girl coping through constant marijuana and sexual objectification.

Vollúpya (Éri Sarmet, Jocimar Dias Jr., Brazil, 20m)

In a post-apocalyptic future, an intergalactic explorer lands at an abandoned museum on a quest to find traces of his long-lost ancestors, and ends up being teleported to the dance floor of a Brazilian queer nightclub in the 1990s.

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Nagarkirtan
films.description: Parimal is a woman trapped in a man’s body who runs away from home and joins a ghetto of eunuchs as Puti and sings at traffic signals to earn money. There she falls in love with Madhu, a delivery boy with a Chinese restaurant who moonlights as a flautist in kirtans. The love blossoms even as Puti dreams of raising the money required for the sex reassignment surgery.

films.title: Naza
films.description:
Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. The film's title - NAZA - is a term that appears throughout the documentary. It is a military acronym euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike.

Directors' Note
We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

— Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

films.title: Necropolis
films.description:
Frankenstein’s monster, Countess Bathory, Attila the Hun, Montezuma, the Devil, witches and other ghosts of history and literature drift through Franco Brocani’s extraordinary NECROPOLIS, a plotless procession of tableaux, monologues and mysterious rituals set somewhere between a ruined civilization and the creative subconscious.

Characters emerge from darkness, deliver delirious confessions and disappear again into a psychedelic labyrinth of bare stages, Pop Art debris and shifting identities. Warhol superstar Viva becomes Bathory, Carmelo Bene plays the Devil, Tina Aumont appears as a witch, and Pierre Clémenti rides naked through the void on a white horse as Attila the Hun, while conversations wander through sex and revolution, religion and magic, madness and death to Gavin Bryars’ hypnotic minimalist score.

Nothing like a conventional horror film but not playing by the rules of any underground cinema either, NECROPOLIS is a strange collision of European avant-garde, theater, performance art and late-’60s counterculture—a lysergic pageant of the monsters, myths and bad dreams left behind by Western civilization.

“I cannot believe I just watched a gorgeous, enigmatic, glacially-paced arthouse film in which Frankenstein’s monster listens to the MC5 while wearing a green velvet suit. How did Franco Brocani know 50 years ago that such a thing was exactly what I needed tonight? Movies are fucking magic.” - Ipsissimu Mocata

films.title: Night of the Living Dead
films.description: The dead come back to life and eat the living. Several people barricade themselves inside a rural house in an attempt to survive the night. Outside are hordes of relentless, shambling zombies who can only be killed by a blow to the head.

films.title: Night of the Vamp-Friars
films.description:
The first feature film wholly produced by Vinegar Syndrome Pictures; directed by Kurtis M. Spieler (Re-Director of New York Ninja).

A group of friends in a punk rock band discover a hidden cemetery in the woods, where they accidentally raise a horde of undead friars.

Shot entirely on 16mm film, Night of the Vamp-Friars is a loving tribute to the homegrown horror films made during the height of the video store era.

Presented with The Grand Illusion.

films.title: No Country for Mothers
films.description:
No Country for Mothers explores the culture wars surrounding American motherhood and why both the “girl boss” and “trad wife” labels ultimately distract us from the real issue: the lack of support for American families. Following activist Reshma Saujani, the film charts a growing national movement to reunite moms across divisions and win the kind of historic support families actually need.

Join us for this family-friendly screening and community event with an age appropriate Q&A, games and activities for kids, and free Molly Moon's Homemade Ice Cream. This isn't just about watching a film; it's about being in a room where we can say things out loud that we've been carrying quietly, and realize we are not alone. We would love for you to join us.

films.title: NT Live: The Misanthrope
films.description:
Award-winner Sandra Oh ("Killing Eve") plays the title role in this razor-sharp reimagining of Molière’s classic dark comedy.

Telling the truth isn’t always that simple. Alice, a brilliant novelist, despises the carefully constructed lies of modern society. But the more she challenges those around her, the fiercer the backlash becomes. Soon, she must confront the price of speaking her truth in a world that would rather silence
her.

Filmed live on stage at the National Theatre, Indhu Rubasingham directs Martin Crimp’s (Cyrano de Bergerac) highly anticipated play.

films.title: PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie
films.description: When their ship gets caught in a storm, the PAW Patrol pups wash up on a tropical island that's teeming with dinosaurs. They soon befriend Rex, a baby dino who's been stranded on the island for years. When Mayor Humdinger's mining plans cause a huge volcano to erupt, the pups spring into action to save Rex's home before everything becomes extinct.

films.title: Poltergeist
films.description:
Strange and creepy happenings beset an average California family, the Freelings -- Steve (Craig T. Nelson), Diane (JoBeth Williams), teenaged Dana (Dominique Dunne), eight-year-old Robbie (Oliver Robins), and five-year-old Carol Ann (Heather O'Rourke) -- when ghosts commune with them through the television set. Initially friendly and playful, the spirits turn unexpectedly menacing, and, when Carol Ann goes missing, Steve and Diane turn to a parapsychologist and eventually an exorcist for help.

Part of the Essential Cinema Series, bringing you films that must be seen on the big screen.

films.title: Practical Magic 2
films.description: The Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all.

films.title: Primetime
films.description: In 2006, "To Catch a Predator" host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

films.title: Real Steel
films.description: Charlie Kenton is a washed-up fighter who retired from the ring when robots took over the sport. After his robot is trashed, he reluctantly teams up with his estranged son to rebuild and train an unlikely contender.

films.title: Rider of the Skulls
films.description:
RIDER OF THE SKULLS has 79 minutes and refuses to waste any of them. A werewolf! A vampire! A witch! Walking skeletons! The Headless Horseman! A corpse resurrected from its coffin to identify its own murderer! Alfredo Salazar’s glorious 1965 horror-western plays like an entire Saturday matinee serial crammed into a single feature, tearing through three supernatural adventures with barely enough time between monsters to reload.

Holding this magnificent pile-up together is a masked charro dressed in black, decorated with skulls and apparently prepared to confront any supernatural menace in Mexico with the same basic equipment he’d use against cattle rustlers. The werewolf transforms from man to skeleton to wolf. The vampire turns into a wonderfully handmade flying bat. A cemetery witch summons the dead. The Headless Horseman brings skeleton henchmen. When bullets don’t work, our hero’s next strategy is generally to keep shooting, start punching or find something with a blade. Nobody questions any of this. Why would they?

Part western, part monster movie, part masked-avenger serial, RIDER OF THE SKULLS has the handmade creatures, foggy graveyards and irresistible comic-book logic of a movie dreamed up without anyone around to say no. It has very little money, three monsters to fight and absolutely no time for restraint.

"A truly sublime artifact. A precious treasure that approaches embodying my platonic ideal of a certain special kind of movie. More than almost any other movie in recent memory, it felt like something that had crawled out of my monstercozy dreams into actual, factual reality. I was transfixed in a kind of awe." - Claire Diane

films.title: Ringu
films.description: When Hideo Nakata’s Ringu first appeared in 1998, it somehow broke containment into the West and spread like a virus, kicking off what would become the J-Horror boom. It’s fitting then that this, the proverbial OG, is about the distribution of a deadly videotape that brings about the wrath of a ghostly little girl who kills anyone who watches it (note to horror movie protagonists: don’t go looking for stuff! You’ll find it). Ringu’s themes of social disconnection and technology in conflict with the resentful past still resonate, but today the VHS vector plays differently, almost as analog’s final assault, angry for being discarded just like the film’s spectral killer.

films.title: RRR
films.description:
Rise! Roar! Revolt!

RRR Asks the question "What if two heroic revolutionary leaders who fought the British Raj had met in real life and teamed up?" Then, the film answers this question with "They would become friends and team up to have insanely awesome battles against the colonizers!"

A film filled with drama, action, fun, and real emotional impact. Featuring seven songs, including the Oscar winning Naatu Naatu, RRR is a theatrical experience like no other and deserving of a visit to the big screen.

Presented in the original Telegu with English subtitles.

films.title: Salome's Last Dance
films.description:
Presented by SIFF and Seattle Opera, in conjunction with their production of "Salome."

On Guy Fawkes Night, Oscar Wilde goes to a luxury brothel where the owner has prepared a surprise for the renowned author: a private and very special performance of his banned play "Salome."

films.title: Scare Package (Shorts)
films.description:
Destiny and desire lead us to nightmarish worlds. A complete package of shorts that delve into body horror, camp, psychosexual fantasy, and the grotesque.

CW: Blood / Gore

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Burning of a Family Tree (Alison Mattingly, United States, 12m)

When Eden returns home to their estranged family after the death of their abusive father, they are forced to confront their traumatic past… and their father’s reanimated corpse.

CW: Religious psychosis

CHASER (Jesse Williams, United Kingdom, 10m)

When Sophia, a trans woman on a night out crosses paths with the seemingly charming Callum, she realizes he may not have her best interest at heart…

CW: Flashing lights

The Dysphoria (Kylie Aoibheann, Australia, 13m)

A trans woman performs a satanic ritual to get a vagina, but unwittingly invites a demonic presence into her home who demands a terrible sacrifice.

Autonecrophile: What It Is To Be An Exquisite Corpse (Maxine Sizemore, United States, 11m)

Based on the filmmakers experience of OCD induced Cotard syndrome, Autonecrophile is an experimental horror short told from the perspective of a conscious dead body who gains the memories of the necrophiliac ex boyfriend who killed her, finding she died long before she wound up in her coffin.

CW: Cancer, necrophilia

Dahlia Has a Phobia (Lenox Myette, United States, 14m)

Two women retreat for a quiet weekend to salvage their unraveling relationship. But when one’s crippling fear of scarecrows resurfaces, their fragile dynamic begins to fracture.

CW: Relational abuse

God Hates a Coward (David Leo, United States, 11m)

A young transgender man goes into a psychosexual spiral after meeting the object of his desires: an aging punk vocalist.

CW: Flashing lights, sexual violence, transphobia

Resurrect Me as a Parasite (Lou Lou Sainsbury & Gabi Dao, Netherlands, 10m)

A vampiric trio facilitates the transition of a new host across a former limestone quarry and the sacred mountain grotto of Mary Magdalene, troubling the binaries of life, death, gender and parasitism.

films.title: Scary Movie
films.description: This film fearlessly spoofs popular movies and trends, delivering a rapid-fire barrage of jokes inspired by Scream, The Sixth Sense, The Matrix, I Know What You Did Last Summer, and The Blair Witch Project. It lampoons familiar teen movie tropes and memorable moments from recent films, television shows, and commercials, pushing the boundaries of parody with a no-holds-barred approach.

films.title: Screamplay
films.description:
“…takes HOLLYWOOD by the throat and STRANGLES it!”

Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies… only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (George Kuchar) instead. When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad.

Inventively produced using a host of early cinematic techniques and featuring a memorable performance by underground film legend George Kuchar, Rufus Butler Seder’s Screamplay is a singularly charming tribute to Old Hollywood and a marvel of low-budget but high-concept filmmaking. New 4K restoration by Muscle Distribution in association with Matchbox Cine.

films.title: Seattle Film Society In Focus: Tyler Michael James
films.description:
The Seattle Film Society's IN FOCUS showcase series returns this October with a screening of Tyler Michael James’s 2022 thriller LOW LIFE!

LOW LIFE follows Benny, a small-time YouTube star who catches predators online, experiences a night from hell when he lets one of them into his own home.

LOW LIFE will be preceded by a screening of the film’s proof-of-concept short, and a conversation about James’s film & career will follow the screening. This event is presented in partnership with the Northwest Film Forum.

Thursday October 15th at the Northwest Film Forum. Doors at 6:30, Film at 7. See you at the movies!

films.title: Session 9
films.description:
25th anniversary screening of one of the more haunting movies of the 21st century. With the composers of the film's score, local experimental music legends Climax Golden Twins, scheduled to join for a live intro and Q&A!

It looms up out of the woods like a dormant beast. Grand, imposing… abandoned and deteriorating, the Danvers State Mental Hospital, closed down for 15 years, is about to receive 5 new visitors. Donning protective gear, the men of the Hazmat Elimination Co. venture into the eerily vast and vacant asylum that is filled with an evil and mysterious past. Rampant patient abuse, medieval medical procedures, and rumors of demonic possession are some of the many dark secrets the hospital holds – but then, so do each of the men.

films.title: Shambhala Story
films.description: In the Himalayan foothills town of Darjeeling, India, a devout Tibetan Buddhist monk named Tashi is sent to Japan to continue his spiritual training. There, he meets a cantankerous elderly man and his parolee granddaughter, Emi. As Tashi grows closer to them, the distance between the lonely Emi and Tashi begins to shrink, and forbidden feelings start to emerge between them.

films.title: Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom
films.description: On Halloween Eve at Mossy Bottom Farm, excitement turns to dismay when the clumsy Farmer ruins the pumpkin patch. Shaun tries fixing it with science experiments, but things go wrong when a wild beast appears in the woods.

films.title: Shrek the Musical
films.description: Shrek the Musical is a one-of-a-kind, hilarious fairy tale in which curses are reversed, monsters get the girls, donkeys and dragons find love, and princesses are beautiful in all shapes and sizes. Grumpy, gruff, green ogre Shrek lives alone in his swamp. The world is fearful and mocking of him, and he is more than happy to leave the world to itself, in turn. Suddenly, his hermit existence is thrown open, when a group of homeless fairy tale characters — Pinocchio, the Gingerbread Man, the Three Little Pigs, and more — burst upon his swamp, seeking refuge from the persecution of the cruel, vertically-challenged Lord Farquaad

films.title: Singin' in the Rain
films.description:
Join us for a very special celebration of the Majestic Bay Theatres' 25th year! We'll kick off the evening with the premiere of a 30 minute documentary telling the story of our theater, before watching one of the very first films we ever showed, Singin' in the Rain! We look forward to celebrating with you!

Gene Kelly, Debbie Reynolds and Donald O'Connor star in one of the greatest musicals ever filmed. Musician Don Lockwood (Kelly) rises to stardom during Hollywood's silent-movie era--paired with the beautiful, jealous and dumb Lina Lamont (Jean Hagen). When Lockwood becomes attracted to young studio singer Kathy Selden (Reynolds), Lamont has her fired. But with the introduction of talking pictures, audiences laugh when they hear Lockwood speak for the first time--and the studio uses Selden to dub her voice. Set during the advent of "talkies," this film classic song-and-dance numbers celebrate the beginning of movie musicals.

films.title: Sleepy Hollow
films.description: Loosely based on Washington Irving's 18th-century horror tale, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, Burton's movie follows a mild-mannered detective named Ichabod Crane (Johnny Depp) in 1799, who is sent to the small town of Sleepy Hollow to investigate a series of supernatural murders.

films.title: Society
films.description:
In remembrance of special effects and makeup artist legend Screaming Mad George, a screening of one of the ickiest, most original body horror shockers of all time.

Teenager Bill Whitney has always felt like the odd one out in his wealthy, upper-class Beverly Hills family. But his sense of alienation takes a sinister turn when he hears an audio recording of his sister’s coming-out party, which seems to implicate his family in a bizarre, ritualistic orgy. Packing stomach-churning grue courtesy of Screaming Mad George and thought-provoking social commentary in equal measure, Brian Yuzna's SOCIETY is a biting satire that culminates in the most gag-inducing “climax” in all of horror history.

films.title: Spookies
films.description:
“A surreal blitz of ooze, slime, hoboes, failed birthday parties, Grim Reapers, explosions, zombies, people jumping through walls, and a guy with his own face silkscreened on his shirt.” — Joseph A. Ziemba, BLEEDING SKULL!

After taking shelter in a spooky old mansion, a group of travelers discover a ouija board and decide to spend the night. But they soon learn that playing with the forces of black magic isn't fun and games, and it's not long before they're battling demonic creatures, shape shifters, and other forms of evil! Of all of the bizarre horror films made in the 1980s, SPOOKIES easily ranks among the weirdest. The film became a fan favorite thanks to its expertly rendered creature effects and notorious for its bizarre production history in which its original creators were fired and replaced by Eugenie Joseph, who added new scenes and re-edited the previously shot footage. Newly restored in 4K from its long lost original negative, SPOOKIES has never looked better.

films.title: Star Trek 2009
films.description: A young and untested crew sets out on the inaugural voyage of the U.S.S. Enterprise, the most advanced starship ever built. Led by James T. Kirk, a spirited and unconventional officer, and his logical Vulcan first officer, Spock, the crew encounters unexpected dangers and conflicts. They must overcome their personal differences and work together to navigate uncharted territory, forming a lasting camaraderie as they explore the galaxy and push the boundaries of human understanding.

films.title: Star Trek Voyager
films.description: Set in 2273, Star Trek: The Motion Picture follows Admiral James T. Kirk as he takes command of the refitted USS Enterprise to intercept a mysterious, world‑destroying alien cloud known as V’Ger, which is on a collision course with Earth

films.title: Stolen Kisses
films.description: As one of his film titles says, François Truffaut is The Man Who Loved Women. He reveres female beauty, intelligence, spirit, wit, and “superior understanding of emotions.” In his films, “Are women magic?” is a recurrent theme. In Truffaut’s Jules and Jim, two men initially see Jeanne Moreau’s Catherine as a statue come to life, but they soon experience her full human complexity. In Stolen Kisses, Truffaut’s cinematic alter-ego, Antoine Doinel (Jean-Pierre Léaud), a romantic who’s endearingly hapless, gains access to the hearts of Paris by taking a detective job. His touching and comic personal private investigations are the most revealing. He’s had a fluctuating romance with violinist Christine (Claude Jade): they never want each other at the same time, but both are still in the game. Antoine is hired by businessman Tabard (Michel Lonsdale) to discover why no one likes him, and is instantly smitten by the man’s elegant wife Fabienne (Delphine Seyrig, a classic New Wave woman). Following the French tradition of an older women giving a younger man his emotional education, she tells the starry-eyed Antoine, “I am not an apparition. I am a woman, unique and irreplaceable.” Meanwhile, young Christine learns that in order to get what you want in life, sometimes you have to give a push.

films.title: Sweeney Todd
films.description: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a “dark operetta” that tells the story of a London barber who seeks revenge on the judge who destroyed his life. Partnering up with Mrs Lovett, owner of the pie shop downstairs, Sweeney slaughters his customers and turns them into pies.

films.title: Take Me Home
films.description: Anna, a 38-year-old Korean adoptee with a cognitive disability, cares for her aging parents in a fragile balance of meeting each others’ needs. When a Florida heat wave shatters their family and Anna’s routine, her future is uncertain - until she creates a world where she can thrive.

films.title: Television Terror Triple Feature Pizza Party 2
films.description:
We invite you once again to make the theater your living room for another trip back in time to the heyday of made-for-TV horror movies.

For this year's triple feature pizza party, we're broadcasting three more chilling tales straight from 1960s, 70s, and 80s network TV, when original horror movies haunted home television screens on a regular basis. The evening's program consists of another trio of lesser-known gems, this time featuring creepy phone calls, stalkers, highway horror, and mysterious items of the occult. As always, the titles are secret, so you won't find out what frightening fables are in store for you until airtime.

Regular concessions will be available for purchase at the beginning of the transmission and throughout the night. The main course will arrive following the first feature. And in addition to satiating the more carnivorous appetites, we’ll have options for our vegetarian and vegan friends too. Plus, during intermissions, you’ll be treated to period-specific Halloween commercials to complete the experience.

films.title: Tenzing
films.description: Based on true events, “Tenzing” chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok), a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston), became the first to summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo), Tenzing finds an ally in expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe). Together, they persuade Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that Tenzing belongs on the British climbing team, rather than merely serving it. Where Western climbers see “Everest” as something to be conquered, Tenzing reveres “Chomolungma” as the sacred mother goddess. What follows is an ascent defined as much by the tensions between backgrounds, classes and competing ambitions as by the perils of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, rank and aspiration fall away, leaving two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — and for Tenzing, the fulfillment of both a lifelong dream and a spiritual calling. Directed by award-winning filmmaker Jennifer Peedom, “Tenzing” is a story of greatness that refuses to be diminished — and the love that makes it possible.

films.title: The Abominable Dr. Phibes
films.description:
Vincent Price is Dr. Anton Phibes: organist, theologian, inventor, presumed-dead widower and the kind of doctor who responds to medical malpractice by constructing an Art Deco murder palace and killing nine doctors according to the Biblical plagues of Egypt. Phibes himself has no face and can’t speak without plugging his neck into a gramophone, but he does have a silent assistant named Vulnavia, a mechanical orchestra and an inexhaustible flair for pageantry.

THE ABOMINABLE DR. PHIBES is a revenge movie dressed for its own funeral, swathed in velvet, clockwork and candlelight and determined to put a lot more bodies in the ground before the service is over. Robert Fuest’s candy-colored nightmare gives Vincent Price one of his greatest roles while perversely denying him the use of his actual voice for most of it. Equal parts horror movie, black comedy and deranged interior-design catalog, PHIBES is macabre, ridiculous, gorgeous and completely committed to the proposition that if you’re going to murder nine people, you might as well make a show out of it.

films.title: The Birch Wood
films.description: Young Stanislaw, riddled with tuberculosis, departs Switzerland to spend his final days with his introverted forester brother Boleshaw on their secluded farm. This return home reignites a sensual passion for life, music, and love, giving him a vibrant energy at odds with his mournful brother. Their conflicting emotions lead to confronting repressed guilt and reconciliation of the past. Set in the early 1930s, this intimate character study offered Wajda the opportunity to explore areas outside of his intensely political war films and contemplate nature through reworking motifs from classic Polish landscape and symbolist paintings in this elegant depiction of early twentieth century provincial life.

films.title: The Blue Rose: Part II
films.description: "Hang onto your light" as we jump head first into the dark nightmare of The Blue Rose. Someone or something is coming out of the forest wrecking havoc in Twin Peaks. The sheriff station is in shambles, the FBI are in over their heads and a darkness is engulfing the small mountain town. Uncover the mystery of the woods and bare witness to a nightmarish homage to David Lynch and the world of "Twin Peaks".

films.title: The Body Snatcher
films.description:
Terror lives in the shadows when it comes to the films conjured from the imagination of Val Lewton, the visionary producer-auteur who turned our fears of the unseen and the unknown into haunting excursions into existential dread. As head of RKO’s B-horror-movie unit during the 1940s, Lewton brought a new sophistication to the genre by wringing chills not from conventional movie monsters but from brooding atmosphere, suggestion, and psychosexual unease. Suffused with ritual, mysticism, and the occult, the poetically hypnotic and the shockingly subversive films are still-tantalizing dreams of death that dare to embrace the darkness.

Based on a story by Robert Louis Stevenson, this spare and chilling entry in Lewton’s oeuvre stars a brilliant Boris Karloff as a struggling cab driver in 19th-century Edinburgh who helps procure bodies from freshly dug graves for a local doctor. Soon enough, the bodies he delivers become a little too fresh. Lewton and director Robert Wise, of course, provide the eerie atmospherics, yet Karloff brings his customary richness of character to this deeply unsettling role, cutting through all the ghoulish murder and blackmail with humor and literate depth as THE BODY SNATCHER builds toward its truly macabre finale.

films.title: The Case of the Three Sided Dream
films.description:
The documentary film on the life and legacy of Rahsaan Roland Kirk – a one of a kind musician, personality, activist and windmill slayer who despite being blind, becoming paralyzed, and facing America’s racial injustices – did not relent.

Co-Presented with Earshot Jazz Festival!

films.title: The Condor Daughter
films.description: Clara is a teenager growing up in a small indigenous community high in the Andes. Her adoptive mother, a midwife who took her in as a baby, has taught her the ancient songs used to guide women through childbirth, melodies passed down for generations, believed to bring new life safely into the world. But while her voice carries on this tradition, her dreams lie elsewhere: she longs to leave the mountains behind and become a folkloric music star in the big city.

films.title: The Cuckoo Clock
films.description: A young woman falls in love with the home-health-care nurse sent to care for her Grandmother with dementia. When the nurse mysteriously disappears, Grandma’s cuckoo clock speaks to her with a warning… Grandma might be responsible.

films.title: The Daytrippers
films.description:
With its droll humor and bittersweet emotional heft, the feature debut of writer-director Greg Mottola announced the arrival of an unassumingly sharp-witted new talent on the 1990s indie film scene. When she discovers a love letter written to her husband (Stanley Tucci) by an unknown paramour, the distraught Eliza (Hope Davis) turns to her tight-knit Long Island family for advice. Soon the entire clan—strong-willed mom (Anne Meara), taciturn dad (Pat McNamara), and jaded sister (Parker Posey) with pretentious boyfriend (Liev Schreiber) in tow—has squeezed into a station wagon and headed into Manhattan to find out the truth, kicking off a one-crazy-day odyssey full of unexpected detours and life-changing revelations. Performed with deadpan virtuosity by a top-flight ensemble cast, The Daytrippers is a wry and piercing look at family bonds stretched to the breaking point.

Screening as a part of our quarterly Staff Selects series! This film was chosen and presented by Camille Hermida-Fuentes, our Director of Operations!

films.title: The Devils
films.description: An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption –and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

films.title: The History of Concrete
films.description: Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series How To with John Wilson, NYC documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world’s most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to tell this seemingly drab story and increase his movie’s appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble—literally and figuratively—as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

films.title: The Hitcher
films.description:
“What do you want?”
"I want you to stop me."

On a dark and stormy night, a fatigued Jim Halsey (C. Thomas Howell), driving cross country from Chicago to deliver a luxury vehicle to its San Diego owner, decides to pick up a mysterious hitchhiker (Rutger Hauer) in West Texas. Hoping for light conversation to fend off drowsiness, Jim ends up with much more than he bargained for: a psychotic killer who whips out a switchblade and dares Jim to stop his killing spree. What follows is a relentlessly sadistic cat-and-mouse nightmare under the unforgiving sun of the American Southwest. Director Robert Harmon utilizes surreal, nightmarish dream logic within the genre framework to deranged ends, putting Jim and his companion Nash (Jennfier Jason Leigh) through the ringer in high gear. The wide open vistas of the desert have never felt so isolating.

35mm print from a private collection.

films.title: The Leopard Man
films.description:
A black leopard escapes into the night, a small New Mexico town grows frightened, and Val Lewton and Jacques Tourneur have everything they need. Adapted from Cornell Woolrich’s Black Alibi and given its wonderfully lurid title by RKO in the wake of CAT PEOPLE, THE LEOPARD MAN turns a simple pulp premise into one of the strangest and most beautifully controlled thrillers of the 1940s—a movie built from darkness, sound, chance and the fear of being alone at exactly the wrong moment.

The final collaboration between Lewton and Tourneur keeps wandering away from the path a conventional mystery might take, following the nighttime life of the town with an almost dreamlike freedom. Ordinary errands and encounters acquire an inexplicable tension. Wind moves through empty streets. Water drips beneath a railroad trestle. Castanets click somewhere in the darkness. Tourneur and cinematographer Robert De Grasse fill the screen with pools of black so deep that simply waiting to discover what might emerge from them becomes almost unbearable, while the soundtrack makes every footstep and distant noise feel potentially significant.

At barely over an hour, THE LEOPARD MAN is lean enough to qualify as pure pulp and strange enough to continually escape its own premise. Beneath the mystery runs the fatalism of Woolrich and Lewton’s fascination with ordinary lives brushing unexpectedly against the unknown, all expressed through filmmaking of extraordinary economy and precision. Manny Farber was already championing it as one of Hollywood’s “original gems” in the early 1950s, and its nocturnal spell has only grown stronger with time. A street, a shadow, a sound in the distance: few horror films have ever needed less to make the darkness feel dangerous.

films.title: The Matrix
films.description: When a beautiful stranger leads computer hacker Neo to a forbidding underworld, he discovers the shocking truth--the life he knows is the elaborate deception of an evil cyber-intelligence.

films.title: The Most Dangerous Game
films.description:
The Sprocket Society presents: a yacht blithely strays into cut-throat terror in this legendary pre-Code thriller, shown with spooky shorts — all on 16mm film!

A secret island owned by a rich, calculating psychopath with unholy kinks. An innocent man and woman thrown together by pure chance, stranded by “accident,” far beyond the help of any caring soul. Frayed wits and a woodsman’s knife pitted against the rich man’s cunning, his arsenal, and his pack of ravening hounds. Ah, the manhunt is on! The bloodlust…so sweet. So perfectly crafted. So inconsequential.

Joel McRae, Fay Wray, and a gloriously villainous Leslie Banks star in a tightly wound thriller that’s as short and hard-hitting as a crossbow bolt.

A low budget studio throw-away, 94 years later it’s been copied countless times yet never bested. Co-helmed by the director of King Kong and shot on the same jungle sets, the tension and fog-choked visuals linger long after the credits roll.

All aboard: your berth awaits!

Presented with selected short subjects.

films.title: The Passenger
films.description:
“What are you running away from?”
“Turn your back to the front seat.”

Lost amidst the deserts of Northern Chad, disaffected American journalist David Locke (Jack Nicholson) stumbles across the dead body of a fellow hotel acquaintance and decides to leave behind more than his sand trapped Land Rover: swapping passports, Locke abandons his identity. Renting a car “for the rest of my life” and embarking on a journey through Germany, England, and Spain, Locke soon discovers that the life he traded in for has direct connections to secret proxy wars and the international arms trade. Accompanied by a young tourist he meets in Barcelona (Maria Schneider), Locke drives further away from himself and the world while being pursued by mysterious criminals and police alike. A maestro of cinematic alienation, Michelangelo Antonioni navigates the slippery nature of identity with impeccable formal control accompanied by a career high point from Jack Nicholson.

“See the film twice and you see two films. See it a third and you see a third. So it goes.” — Robert Koehler, CinemaScope

35mm print courtesy of Sony Pictures Classics

films.title: The Phantom of the Opera
films.description:
A young soprano becomes the obsession of a disfigured and murderous musical genius who lives beneath the Paris Opéra House.

Every movie starts with a story at the North Bend Theatre. Just prior to each of the Love & War movies, our resident film experts, Kevin & Beth, will share the amazing stories behind these great films, giving you a whole new way to connect to the movie.

films.title: The Promised Land
films.description: Set during the Industrial Revolution in 19th century Łódź, three entrepreneurial friends pool their resources to open a textile factory. But friendships, personal relationships and moral values are soon tested when they encounter ruthlessly competitive barons and competing self interests. An adaptation of Nobel Prize-winning author Stanisław Reymont’s novel, the film is a compelling and continually pertinent indictment of rampant capitalism and humanity’s more selfish impulses. Wajda’s first Academy Award-nominated drama remains one of his most celebrated films.

films.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
films.description:
Rocky Horror is back at the North Bend Theatre!

In this cult classic, sweethearts Brad (Barry Bostwick) and Janet (Susan Sarandon), stuck with a flat tire during a storm, discover the eerie mansion of Dr. Frank-N-Furter (Tim Curry), a transvestite scientist. As their innocence is lost, Brad and Janet meet a houseful of wild characters, including a rocking biker (Meat Loaf) and a creepy butler (Richard O'Brien). Through elaborate dances and rock songs, Frank-N-Furter unveils his latest creation: a muscular man named "Rocky."

films.title: The Scout
films.description:
Sofia works as a location scout for a TV pilot filming in New York City. It’s her job to find the homes, businesses, and exteriors where the show will be filmed. Driving around the city's different neighborhoods, she enters the private spaces of strangers to photograph their cozy apartments and eclectic shops, stepping into the fabric of their lives while trying to satisfy the demands of her erratic employers. Over a day filled with these encounters, Sofia witnesses moments of curiosity, vulnerability, and quiet tension until her work takes a sudden, personal turn. Drawing from her own experience as a location scout, writer-director Paula González-Nasser captures the poetry and costs of being a young creative. Her celebrated directorial debut The Scout crafts a contemplative exploration of urban disconnection, following one woman's journey through other people's worlds as she struggles to find her own.

Alumni of the 2016 edition of NFFTY, filmmakers Paula González-Nasser and Ryan Martin Brown will be in conversation with NFFTY Program Manager Amy Williams following the film. Special youth pricing (24 & younger) is available for the 10/9 screening.

films.title: The Shining
films.description: A struggling writer, Jack Torrance, accepts a winter caretaker position at the isolated Overlook Hotel in the Colorado Rockies, hoping the solitude will overcome his writer's block. He brings his wife, Wendy, and their young son, Danny. However, the hotel harbors a dark history, and as Jack becomes increasingly isolated by the heavy snowfall, he slowly descends into madness, threatening his family and uncovering terrifying secrets within the Overlook's walls

films.title: The Totally Halloween Sing Along
films.description:
This is Halloween; everybody make a scene.

It's a night of your favorite spooky songs and deathly dance hits, all with the lyrics on the big scream screen. Come in costume or come as you are for a monsterously good time, for no mere mortal can resist an evening of the Sing Along...

films.title: The Vanishing
films.description:
A young Dutch couple stops at a crowded highway service station in France. Saskia goes inside to buy drinks and never comes back. From that frighteningly simple premise, George Sluizer builds one of the most unnerving thrillers ever made—a movie that can turn a gas station in broad daylight into a place you’ll never quite trust again.

THE VANISHING is a marvel of restraint, stripping away nearly everything we expect a thriller to use for suspense. Sluizer doesn’t even hide the man responsible. Instead, we watch Raymond—an ordinary husband, father and chemistry teacher—rehearse conversations, measure time with a stopwatch and methodically prepare for an unspeakable act. Bernard-Pierre Donnadieu’s astonishingly matter-of-fact performance makes him more disturbing with every mundane detail, while Sluizer finds menace in cars, coffee, coins, parking lots and vacation homes. There are no monsters here, no elaborate shocks and almost no violence. There is simply the growing realization that something horrifying can happen in the middle of an ordinary day and leave behind nothing but a question.

Three years after Saskia disappears, Rex still needs the answer to that question. Soon we do too. That shared need to know is where THE VANISHING becomes truly merciless, tightening curiosity into dread with the precision of a trap closing one click at a time. Stanley Kubrick was reportedly so disturbed and fascinated by the film that he contacted Sluizer to discuss how it worked, and its reputation has only grown since. Cold without being clinical, psychologically acute without becoming cerebral, THE VANISHING is the rare thriller whose power comes not from what it hides, but from how desperately it makes you want to see it.

films.title: The Way Out
films.description: The Way Out drops you right into the action across the globe, from heavy Alaskan spine lines to local backyard laps in Whistler. The Way Out represents a path toward total freedom. Whether tracking Hoji, Chris Rubens, and Mark Abma across the iconic Swiss Alps or capturing breakout skier Lucy Leishman storming through Japan’s deep powder with three legendary freeskiers, the verdict is simple: the soul of skiing isn’t dead; it's alive and well wherever the snow is falling.

films.title: The Wedding
films.description: An intellectual poet and peasant woman unite in matrimony, with their wedding party attended by a class-crossing assortment of society. However, the veneer of harmony is broken when ghosts – drawn from local history and legend – appear out of the fog to the revellers. Wajda’s psychedelic adaptation of Stanisław Wyspiański’s influential 1901 play where (as stated in the prologue) “everything in [the] story is true —even the dreams,” employs dizzying cinematography and creates an eerie atmosphere to offer a searing critique of the nation’s phantoms. It became one of the most culturally significant works of Polish cinema.

films.title: Traces of Home
films.description: Delving into the past and not shying away from the dug-up pain, a young filmmaker speaks to her Mexican mother and Palestinian father about their trying journeys into the United States. In a society with rhetoric increasingly vilifying Mexicans and Palestinians, the filmmaker picks up her camera in a bid to address the grief at the center of the generational trauma that has underscored her relationship with her family. A meditation of loss and grief relieved, ultimately, through reconciliation.

films.title: Train to Busan
films.description:
Seok-woo is a workaholic dad who has trouble bonding with his young daughter Su-an. For her birthday, she wants to visit her mother in Busan. After seeing how he's been neglecting her feelings, he agrees and accompanies her on the train ride across the country.

Then, the world falls apart.

And Seok-woo transforms from an absent father to a devoted dad with one mission: to make sure his daughter survives.

Met with worldwide acclaim, Train To Busan balances a cast of well-rounded characters with suspense and bursts of visceral action, all while weaving in social commentary for a refreshing take on the zombie genre.

Presented in the original Korean language with English subtitles.

films.title: Trans Panic!
films.description:
A Christian trans hyperpop musician teams up with an intersex incel filmmaker on a mad plan involving performative terrorism, career-launching martyrdom, and a chaotic love triangle that might include JD Vance. This film asks: What if your intersectionality intersected with evil and made you suck a lot?

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Trans-It (Shorts)
films.description:
The mode in which we journey from one place to another, physically and emotionally. Public transport, psychic transferrence, and personal transmutation. All aboard!

FILMS IN THIS PROGRAM:

Mascott (Marilyne Lamontagne, Canada, 13m)

A struggling transgender actor lands a bear mascot role on a children’s TV show, but as fame, hyper-masculinity, and public expectations close in, the bear suit refuses to come off.

As the time might be now (Noah Mancini, Zuma Link, Brazil, 16m)

On a feverish night, Dama da Noite crosses the city carrying a deck of cards that could change her fate. Between picturesque bars, collapsing apartments, and unlikely encounters, her path crosses with Onça, a young man adrift through the night.

How to Become Transgender In Order to Dodge the American Military Draft (Dustin Wilson V, Joschua Stice, United States, 6m)

Follows the creation and distribution of a flyer, instructing the residents of Seattle on how to dodge the draft.

How to Find a Career That Loves You Back (Ethernet Wang, United States, 25m)

Khloe, an isolated young trans woman, works for Scryr, a defense-technology startup that uses AI to militarize surveillance. Khloe questions the violence of her work, and as intrusive thoughts become intolerable, a decision presents itself.

Metamórfike (LUI NASCIMENTO, Brazil, 15m)

Lolo is a young non-binary person, influencer, and music video director who works as a delivery rider around the city. After receiving a mysterious delivery, strange things begin. A tropical queer sci-fi through the streets of Belo Horizonte, Brazil.

They Persist (Lachlan Salvestro, Australia, 8m)

A short film about the forever stagnant versions of ourselves that exist in the hearts and minds of the people we’ve left behind, as we grow and move on with our lives.

They Persist (Lachlan Salvestro, Australia, 8m)

A short film about the forever stagnant versions of ourselves that exist in the hearts and minds of the people we’ve left behind, as we grow and move on with our lives.

While construction is in progress, shops will remain open (Mordred Guadagno, France, 2m)

Between 2021 and 2025, a city was under massive construction preparing for a new streetcar line. As work finally come to an end, a parallel construction of the self is grappled with.

films.title: True Stories
films.description:
There is perhaps no film to come out of the Reagan era that is as optimistic and positive about American life than David Byrne’s True Stories.

Inspired by absurd tabloid clippings he collected while on tour with Talking Heads with the question of “what if this was all true,” Byrne managed to create a collage of average middle-American life that elevates its subjects to the extraordinary. Moving between computer chip plants, mall fashion shows, and basement Voodou rituals, True Stories becomes the inverse of a film like David Lynch’s Blue Velvet (released the same year!) in that it seeks to find the good hidden underneath the (sometimes) hard exterior of American life deep in the heart of Texas.

films.title: TV Party: Doomed Occult Detectives
films.description:
For a brief, beautiful period in the ’60s and ’70s, television kept trying to invent the guy you called when the police couldn’t help. Ghost hunters, psychic investigators, demonologists, and occult experts armed with ancient books, skeptical assistants and suspiciously helpful police contacts, they were built to spend every week cracking another impossible case. Before KOLCHAK went chasing monsters through the night and long before THE X-FILES put the paranormal on the federal payroll, these would-be series were already trying to turn the venerable occult detective of weird fiction into a weekly television hero. Networks commissioned the pilots, watched them…and repeatedly decided there would be no Episode Two.

TV PARTY exhumes two of the best surviving specimens: a mystery double feature of orphaned pilots from series that never existed, each introducing a brand-new supernatural sleuth and sending him straight into his first—and last—case. Expect haunted houses, impossible murders, forbidden artifacts, black magic and two tantalizing glimpses of the horror shows television almost gave us. No titles until showtime. The networks buried them. We’re putting them back on the air.

films.title: Two-Lane Blacktop
films.description:
An unnamed drag racing duo (James Taylor and "The Beach Boys"' Dennis Wilson, referred to as The Driver and Mechanic in novelist Rudy Wurlitzer’s screenplay) head eastward from Los Angeles in their souped up ‘55 Chevy. They cross paths with an orbit-orange GTO and its wandering loner of a driver played by Warren Oates, bedecked throughout in a kaleidoscope wardrobe of cashmere sweaters. Vying for the attention of a restless hitchhiker in tow (Laurie Bird), the trio embark on a race for pink slips across six southern states. Filmed in sequence and entirely on location, Monte Hellman’s low budget masterpiece of highway philosophy features gorgeous widescreen photography and sparse, existential dialogue that captures a moment in time when, as Vincent Canby states, “faith in God is a lot less important, less immediate and even less mystical than faith in the internal combustion engine.” The quintessential American road film.

“In Two-Lane Blacktop [the road] becomes something altogether different and far more interesting: a repository of dreams and fantasies, for squares, hipsters, and obsessives alike…It is a movie about loneliness, and the attempts made by people to connect with one another and maintain their solitude at the same time—an impossible task, an elusive dream.” — Kent Jones

films.title: Understanding Myself as an Amphibian
films.description:
Understanding Myself as an Amphibian is a Queer ecology feature documentary exploring sexual diversity in wildlife, drawing connections between incredible species and the director’s own journey. The film is an enlightening reflection on wildlife and the influences affecting our understanding of animal and human behaviour.

Screens with the short film Objectionable Fruit!

(Hogan Seidel & Gabby Follett, United States, 15m)

Objectionable Fruit is an experimental four channel 16mm documentary short examining the Ginkgo tree—a living fossil celebrated for its resilience and unique capacity to change sexes, defying human-imposed binaries.

CW: Flashing lights

films.title: Universal Monster Mash Double Feature
films.description:
Featuring FRANKENSTEIN MEETS THE WOLF MAN and ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN!

Universal spent the 1930s turning Dracula, Frankenstein’s Monster and the Wolf Man into movie stars. Then somebody had the bright idea to start putting them in each other’s movies. This double feature catches the Universal monster rally at its beginning and its glorious peak: first the movie that brought two horror franchises crashing together, then the one that let Abbott and Costello hang out in the wreckage.

It starts with poor Larry Talbot. All the Wolf Man wants is to die. Instead, grave robbers dig him up, the full moon brings him back to life, and his search for a permanent cure leads him straight to the frozen body of Frankenstein’s Monster. FRANKENSTEIN MEETS THE WOLF MAN piles on foggy graveyards, ruined castles, terrified villagers, mad science, Bela Lugosi in neck bolts, Lon Chaney Jr. suffering beautifully and a cheerful musical number called “Life Is Short, but Death Is Long” before finally delivering on the promise of its title: two monsters beating the hell out of each other while the laboratory comes down around them.

Five years later, Universal decided what this situation needed was Lou Costello. Dracula wants his brain for Frankenstein’s Monster. The Wolf Man wants to stop Dracula. Bud Abbott doesn’t believe any of this is happening. And Bela Lugosi, returning to Dracula for the first time since 1931, treats the whole ridiculous situation with the dignity of a bloodsucking aristocrat whose evil scheme does not involve two vaudeville comedians. ABBOTT AND COSTELLO MEET FRANKENSTEIN somehow lets the monsters remain scary, Abbott and Costello remain funny, and both movies occupy the same frame without anybody blinking. Dracula turns into a bat. The Wolf Man goes through a window. Frankenstein’s Monster throws a woman out another window. And when the dust settles, Universal has somehow made one of its funniest comedies and one of its greatest monster movies at the same time.

Two movies, five years apart, tracing one of the happiest developments in horror history: Universal turning its stable of monsters into the world’s ugliest repertory company.

films.title: Unzipped
films.description:
Both a time capsule of the buoyant, raucous 1990s, when pop culture and high art became interchangeable, and a vérité-style, in-the-trenches report on the daily agonies and ecstasies of the creative process, this seminal artistic portrait—sumptuously shot by Ellen Kuras and Robert Leacock—transcends glitz and glamour to offer an extraordinary view of the charisma and force of will inherent to genius, as well as its personal costs.

Digitally restored by the Sundance Institute and UCLA Film & Television Archive. Funding provided by Isaac Mizrahi Entertainment. Laboratory services by Roundabout Entertainment, Inc. and Deluxe Media Audio Services.

films.title: Verity
films.description: Lowen Ashleigh is hired by Jeremy Crawford to ghostwrite novels for his bestselling author wife Verity, who is unable to finish following an accident. Lowen gradually uncovers Verity's disturbing truths while residing at the Crawfords' home to work.

films.title: Vertigo
films.description:
James Stewart stars as a retired San Francisco detective who takes on a case to follow an old friend's wife, only to spiral deeper into an obsession with her.

Considered one of Hitchcock's finest. Stewart is in top form as he falls further into madness.

films.title: VHS Über Alles Presents...
films.description:
SHOT ON VIDEO HALLOWEEN SPECIAL!

Experience cult movies in analog glory! Seattle’s ultimate VHS screening series delivers an unstoppable onslaught of 0.5-inch magnetic power. All we can tell you about the film is this:

A HORRIFYING DESCENT INTO THE TWISTED KILLING SPREE OF A PSYCHOPATH!

Just $5 gets you a seat before we hit “play” on the all-powerful VCR.

films.title: Videodrome
films.description:
Annual William Kennedy Memorial Screening of the David Cronenberg classic!

When Max Renn goes looking for edgy new shows for his sleazy cable TV station, he stumbles across the pirate broadcast of a hyperviolent torture show called Videodrome. As he struggles to unearth the origins of the program, he embarks on a hallucinatory journey into a shadow world of right-wing conspiracies, sadomasochistic sex games, and bodily transformation. Starring James Woods and Debbie Harry, with groundbreaking special effects makeup by Rick Baker, VIDEODROME is one of David Cronenberg’s most original and provocative works, fusing social commentary with shocking elements of sex and violence.

Back in June 2021, Seattle lost one of its most dedicated cinephiles, William Kennedy. One of Bill’s final wishes was that people gather to watch VIDEODROME in his memory. A portion of the proceeds from this screening will be donated to Evergreen Playhouse in Centralia, where Bill performed in several productions prior to moving to Seattle.

films.title: Wagon Master
films.description:
A picaresque road poem, Wagon Master remained a personal favorite of John Ford’s amongst his own pictures and one of three that “came closest to being what I wanted to achieve.” Nearly plotless with an emphasis on grace notes, this relaxed film charts the journey of two horse traders with a shared yen for adventure who are hired by Elder Wiggs (Ward Bond) to lead a Mormon wagon train through southeastern Utah. Along the way they encounter a theater troupe, sex workers, lawmen, Indigenous peoples, and ornery outlaws on the run, all of whom find themselves brought in as members of the traveling community through what Harvard Film Archive calls an “almost musical combination, separation and recombination.” Deceptively simple and elegant in construction, Ford shot this lyrical and visually rapturous film away from his usual commanding landscapes of Monument Valley, instead emphasizing the beauty of a multicultural motley crew of outcasts on the dusty trail.

“Seldom has the western landscape seemed such a tangible emblem of hope and freedom. A masterpiece beyond question — but a masterpiece that never degenerates into pomposity or self-consciousness. It's American filmmaking at its finest and most eloquent." — Dave Kehr, Chicago Reader

“Wagon Master is more poetry than drama…less interested in where it is going (plot), than in where it is (the moment). Still, obviously, it is a movie about passage, a ‘parade’ West. Only briefly is ‘home,’ the antithesis of passage, suggested.” — Tag Gallagher

35mm print courtesy of Park Circus

films.title: We Live!!! (Shorts)
films.description:

Luna, a young transfeminine woman, attends her family’s annual Chinese New Year gathering for the first time since her transition.

A portrait of an LGBT weightlifting club in Sheffield, exploring the embodiment of queer and trans power.

Swann Queen (L cedeño miller, United States, 11m)

At a ball hosted by the world’s first drag queen, the category is: run or resist.

May Everything Trans/form (Frankie Murphy, United States, 2m)

A lo-fi Neruda poem.

films.title: Whalefall
films.description: Following the death of his father (Josh Brolin), Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) goes diving off the central Coast of California in search of his remains, but is swallowed by a massive sperm whale. While trapped inside its belly with only one hour of oxygen left, Jay comes to realize that the hard-earned lessons his father imparted may be the key to his escape.

films.title: What the River Knows
films.description: Today, a lost Eden emerges from beneath Lake Powell, revealing both the consequences of past mistakes and the potential for a new path forward for the Colorado River. What The River Knows explores this pivotal moment, where the urgent need to rethink water management in the West aligns with an opportunity to restore a stunning landscape and flooded ancestral homeland. Amidst the grim discussions surrounding climate change and the Colorado River crisis, the film tells a powerful story of nature’s resilience: Glen Canyon is coming back to life.

films.title: Who Moves America
films.description: As the world’s largest package delivery company, UPS moves millions of packages across more than 200 countries and territories each day – and its workforce holds the power to bring that machine to a halt. Who Moves America follows a UPS driver in California casting his first strike vote, a Teamster in New York who walked the picket line during the historic 1997 strike, and a warehouse worker in Kentucky balancing night shifts with community college, weighing whether she can afford to say no, as well as access to the General President of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Sean O’Brien. As they and their co-workers organize, argue, and campaign across the country, the film builds toward a single, high-stakes vote: accept the deal, or risk everything for a strike that could reshape the American economy. Through intimate access and on-the-ground storytelling, Who Moves America reveals the human stories behind the single largest collective bargaining agreement in North America and explores the power and complexity of collective action in modern America.

films.title: Wicker
films.description: An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, Wicker tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Alexander Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life.

films.title: Wildwood
films.description: After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

films.title: Withdrawal
films.description:
Writer/director/editor Aaron Strand scheduled to join for an in-person intro and Q&A. Raw, unflinching, and surprisingly funny, WITHDRAWAL was shot on miniDV in Athens, GA for a budget of $60k and is a prime example of indie filmmaking at its finest.

Artistic lovers Viv (Millie Rose Evans) and Jay (Brent Michal) are trapped in a vicious cycle of codependent heroin addiction. When Viv's wealthy parents hire an interventionist to take her to rehab, the couple decides to go it alone with nothing but a suboxone prescription and each other. All they have to do is survive one harrowing night of withdrawal. As the hours tick by, physical, mental, and emotional torments send them searching through fractured memories, trying to figure out where it all went wrong.

Winner of a dozen awards on the festival circuit, including Best Feature/Best Director at the Art of Brooklyn Film Festival and Best Actress at the Kanazawa Film Festival.

films.title: You Can See Everything
films.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.

films.title: Young Frankenstein
films.description: Following in the footsteps of his infamous grandfather, Dr. Frederick Frankenstein inherits his ancestor's Transylvanian castle and laboratory. He initially attempts to distance himself from the family's legacy, but is drawn into recreating the experiments that brought his grandfather's monster to life. With the help of Igor, the bubbly Inga, and the unsettling Frau Blücher, Frederick’s plans are complicated by a living monster and the unexpected arrival of his fiancée, Elizabeth, leading to chaotic and hilarious consequences.
